title.narrative: Integrated multi-sector intervention for conflict-affected populations in Aba’ala Woreda, Zone 2, Afar

description.narrative: ltpgtIn regions reeling from the aftermath of conflict and drought, multifaceted initiatives are crucial to mitigate immediate hardships and nurture long-term resilience. Mercy Corps Ethiopia, with national partner, Friendship Support Association, propose a $1,000,000 integrated, multi- sector response, providing life-saving assistance to 67,291 individuals affected by drought and conflict in communities of Aba'ala woreda in Zone 2, Afar, especially for nutritionally vulnerable groups like pregnant and lactating women and children under five, concentrating on Education, MPCA, Protection, WASH, and Agriculture.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtIn Aba’ala, the tailored MPCA program steps in to alleviate immediate and sustained hardships by providing enhanced cash transfers and nutritional literacy training. The program is structured, focusing on immediate relief and long-term impact, and is undertaken in collaboration with local banks to instill self-reliance and empower communities, especially focusing on nutritionally vulnerable groups.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtSimultaneously, the Protection sector is the lifeline for individuals, predominantly women and children, affected by conflict and disaster, aiming to mitigate suffering, restore dignity, and ensure safety through services like client-centered GBV case management and establishment of women and girls’ safe spaces. The project also provides strategic cash assistance and capacity-building support for service providers, focusing on empowering communities and integrating psychological support.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe WASH sector stands as a pillar to reduce morbidity and mortality by rendering resilient services to school communities and those affected by disruptions and conflicts. The initiatives in this sector are targeted to enhance water supply, restore energy, and ensure comprehensive water purification, coupled with holistic hygiene promotion to foster healthy behaviors and prevent disease propagation.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtOur initiatives in Agriculture seek to foster sustainable agrarian practices and improve food security through innovative and eco-friendly farming techniques, efficient water management, and community engagement, focusing on enhancing crop diversity and yield, ultimately leading to community resilience.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThese interventions, collectively, are not merely stopgap measures. They are designed to lay the foundation for sustainable development and long-lasting recovery, integrating immediate life-saving actions with enduring solutions. Every initiative taken is designed to create substantial, sustainable impacts, emphasizing empowerment, economic resilience, psychological well-being, and community integration. ltspangtThis approach not only alleviates immediate hardships but also instills knowledge and resources needed for long-term resilience and self-reliance, contributing meaningfully to community revitalization, resilience, and empowerment in crisis-impacted areas.lt/spangtlt/pgt
